summary: Colin Leslie Dean is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria.
Colin Mackenzie (1754–1821) studied at Dollar Academy and worked in indology, history, and archaeology. From 1810 to 1815, he served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India.

Colin Turnbull (1924–1994) was a religious studies scholar. He was educated at Westminster School (around 1938–1942), Magdalen College (around 1942–1947), and Banaras Hindu University (around 1949–1951).

Collett Cox, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a PhD at Columbia under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda, and studied at Tokyo and Ryukoku. She held a professorship at the University of Washington (attested 1999–2026).
Conor Roddy is a philosopher who completed a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011), having studied under teachers Arindam Chakrabarti and Roger T. Ames.

Conrad Bursian (1830–1883) studied at Leipzig and Berlin. A scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields, he held posts at Leipzig (~1856–1861), Tübingen (~1861–1864), Zurich (~1864–1869), Jena (~1869–1874), and Munich (~1874–1883).

Conrad M. Arensberg (1910–1997) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Harvard University (~1927–1934) and held a post at Columbia University from approximately 1946 to 1979.

Constance Kassor is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. After earning a BA at Smith College and a PhD at Emory University under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, she joined the Smith College faculty (attested 2014).
Constance Powell Chin is an archaeologist and religious studies scholar who earned a master's degree at San Jose State University by 2012, having studied under Christian Luczanits.

Constantin Regamey (1907–1982) was an indologist, tibetologist, and linguist educated at Warsaw (PhD ~1935) and Paris. He taught at Warsaw (1936), Fribourg (1945), and Lausanne (1945; extraordinary professor 1949–1957), and served as Swiss Asia Society president (1962–1971).

Corinna May Lhoir works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Attested in 2026, she is a PhD student at Ghent University, a doctoral researcher at the University of Hamburg, and a yoga studies program coordinator and lecturer at Hamburg.

Cornelis Jan Kuiken is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. Supervised for his MA by Jaap den Hollander, he completed a PhD at the University of Groningen in 2002 under Timothy H. Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) studied at the Remonstrant Seminary and University of Amsterdam. A scholar of religious studies and history, he was a professor at the Remonstrant Seminary (1873) and held the history of religions chair at Leiden (1877–1901).

Corrado Pensa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Raniero Gnoli and Giuseppe Tucci. He served as Professor of Religions and Philosophy of India and the Far East at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1971).

Cortland Dahl is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and received mentorship from Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.

Courtney Bruntz works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She served as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015) and later as a professor of East Asian Buddhism at the Numata Center (attested 2026).

Craig Jamieson is an indologist and Buddhist studies specialist. He served as a fellow at Queens' College, Cambridge, and worked at the University of Cambridge (attested 2002), including as curator of its South Asia manuscript collection (attested 2012).
Craig Preston is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Virginia under Joe Bransford Wilson and Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981).

Cristina Pecchia studied at Sapienza University of Rome (PhD ~1999–2003) and the University of Vienna. Active in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, she worked as a researcher at IKGA (~2008) and as a lecturer at the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Csaba Dezső (born 1973) is an indologist who earned master's degrees at Eötvös Loránd University (~1992–1997) and a PhD at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1998–2004). He served as an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University around 2003.
